knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A documented practice that the business actually runs, with evidence, is a claim that can be checked. Vague superlatives, competitor criticism and brand promises are not evidence.
Slow trust means fewer early repeat clients, so the business should plan time and cash for that period. It does not mean stopping marketing or setting prices by default.
A foreign, dated statistic is a hypothesis for local testing. Removing all market analysis or quoting the figure to customers both misuse the source.

practicalCriteria: Three customer needs are written as observable behaviours.
Interview notes are recorded for at least ten prospects or recent clients, each with a date.
Competitor map has the same four columns for every competitor type.
Each trust claim in the draft message is matched to a filed record.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark (all 3 of 3 correct for this lesson). A quiz pass is not verified practical competence. The needs list, interview notes and competitor map are assessed separately by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Interview notes and competitor map reviewed by an assessor
Trust evidence folder with a record for each claim
stopWorkCriteria: Stop publishing any trust, safety or results claim that has no filed record.
Stop using any external statistic as a local fact before it has been tested locally.
